items.stem: Which of the following best describes "potentiometer (variable potential divider)"?
options: The number of free charge carriers per unit volume, n, in m⁻³
A circuit in which components are connected end to end so that the same current flows through each
A component whose resistance decreases as the intensity of light falling on it increases
A resistor with a sliding contact used to give a continuously variable output pd
items.answer: A resistor with a sliding contact used to give a continuously variable output pd
items.markingKey: D. "potentiometer (variable potential divider)" is a resistor with a sliding contact used to give a continuously variable output pd.

items.stem: A teacher in Cape Town asks a class to choose the one correct statement about isovolumetric, isobaric, isothermal and adiabatic processes on p-V diagrams. Which statement should be chosen?
options: Supplying heat to a gas always increases its temperature.
A system contains a certain amount of heat.
In the Carnot efficiency formula, temperatures can be in °C.
Isobaric means constant pressure; work pΔV is done if the volume changes. Isovolumetric processes involve no work.
items.answer: Isobaric means constant pressure; work pΔV is done if the volume changes. Isovolumetric processes involve no work.
items.markingKey: D. The other options are common misconceptions. Isobaric means constant pressure; work pΔV is done if the volume changes. Isovolumetric processes involve no work.

items.stem: Aiko travels from Earth to Gliese 581 (20.4 ly in Earth’s frame) at 0.5c. Calculate the journey time in years measured by Aiko’s clock.
items.answer: 35.3 years
items.markingKey: C. Earth time = 20.4/0.5 = 40.8 y (M1); proper time = Earth time/γ = 35.3 y (A1).

items.stem: A tram in Vienna reaches 6 m s⁻¹ from rest in 3 s and later stops from 6 m s⁻¹ in 3 s, both uniformly. Calculate the magnitude of the deceleration while stopping.
items.markingKey: B. Deceleration = gradient of the v–t graph = 6/3 (M1) = 2.00 m s⁻² (A1).

items.stem: A parachutist falls at terminal velocity. Which statement is correct?
options: The drag force equals the weight
The drag force is greater than the weight
items.answer: The drag force equals the weight
items.markingKey: B. Zero resultant force at constant velocity.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "temperature"?
options: A state of matter (solid, liquid or gas) with uniform physical properties
A measure of the average random kinetic energy of the particles of a substance; the absolute temperature in kelvin is proportional to it
A phase in which particles vibrate about fixed positions and are held close together by strong intermolecular forces
The total random kinetic energy and intermolecular potential energy of the particles in a substance
items.answer: A measure of the average random kinetic energy of the particles of a substance; the absolute temperature in kelvin is proportional to it
items.markingKey: B. "temperature" is a measure of the average random kinetic energy of the particles of a substance; the absolute temperature in kelvin is proportional to it.

items.stem: Noah is revising electrical power and energy. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Current is greater in the first resistor of a series circuit and then decreases.
Power depends on both V and I (P = VI); a high-voltage device with a small current can have low power.
The power dissipated in a resistor always increases with its resistance.
Connecting a lower external resistance always gives more power to the load.
items.answer: Power depends on both V and I (P = VI); a high-voltage device with a small current can have low power.
items.markingKey: B. The other options are common misconceptions. Power depends on both V and I (P = VI); a high-voltage device with a small current can have low power.

items.stem: Tariq rides a bicycle at 10 m s⁻¹ in Mexico City. The wheels have radius 0.33 m and roll without slipping. Calculate the angular velocity of the wheels.
items.answer: 30.3 rad s⁻¹
items.markingKey: C. ω = v/r (M1) = 30.3 rad s⁻¹ (A1).

items.stem: A grandfather clock in Mumbai needs a pendulum with a period of 3.0 s. Calculate the required length.
A teacher in Lima asks a class to choose the one correct statement about displacement-distance and displacement-time graphs of waves. Which statement should be chosen?
options: A larger amplitude wave travels faster.
Increasing the frequency of a wave increases its speed.
Waves transfer matter from one place to another.
At a crest the displacement is maximum and the point is momentarily at rest; points at equilibrium move fastest.
items.answer: At a crest the displacement is maximum and the point is momentarily at rest; points at equilibrium move fastest.
items.markingKey: D. The other options are common misconceptions. At a crest the displacement is maximum and the point is momentarily at rest; points at equilibrium move fastest.

items.stem: The unit of entropy is
items.answer: J K⁻¹
items.markingKey: C. ΔS = Q/T.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about work done by a force and the work-energy principle is a common misconception? (Revision quiz set by Mohammed.)
options: Energy density = specific energy × density; hydrogen has a very high specific energy but, being very low in density, a low energy density.
mgh only gives the change in GPE close to Earth’s surface where g is uniform; for large distances the field varies.
Typical efficiencies are 35–55 %; most energy is transferred to the surroundings as thermal energy in cooling towers and flue gases.
Holding a heavy object still is hard work, so a lot of work is done on it.
items.answer: Holding a heavy object still is hard work, so a lot of work is done on it.
items.markingKey: D. This is incorrect: Muscles use chemical energy (internal processes) but no work is done on the object because it does not move.

items.stem: A fixed mass of air in a bicycle pump at 1.00 × 10⁵ Pa occupies 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ m³. It is compressed slowly at constant temperature to 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ m³. Calculate the new pressure.
items.markingKey: D. p₁V₁ = p₂V₂ (M1); p₂ = 4.00 × 10⁵ Pa (A1).

items.stem: A gas absorbs 1200 J of thermal energy while doing 150 J of work on its surroundings. Calculate the change in its internal energy.
items.markingKey: B. ΔU = Q − W with W = 150 J (M1); ΔU = 1050 J (A1).

items.stem: Ingrid writes four statements while revising real gases versus ideal gases. Which one is a misconception?
options: Ideal gases exist at room temperature.
Real gases deviate at high pressure and low temperature, where molecular volume and intermolecular forces matter.
The gas laws apply to a fixed amount of gas; if n changes, pV/T changes in proportion.
Above its critical temperature a gas cannot be liquefied by pressure alone.
items.answer: Ideal gases exist at room temperature.
items.markingKey: A. This is incorrect: No gas is exactly ideal; some (He, H₂, N₂) are very close to ideal at everyday conditions.

items.stem: Which of the following is a good example of approximate SHM?
options: A ball rolling in a V-shaped trough
A car moving in a circle
A pendulum swinging through a small angle
items.answer: A pendulum swinging through a small angle
items.markingKey: D. Small angle approximation.

items.stem: Diego writes four statements while revising postulates of special relativity and Lorentz transformations. Which one is a misconception?
options: Any frame moving at constant velocity is inertial; there is no experiment that distinguishes rest from uniform motion.
Relativistic effects only appear because clocks are badly made.
In her own frame everything is normal: her heartbeat and clocks run at the usual rate; it is the observer in another frame who measures her clocks running slow.
With ct vertical, a steeper worldline means a smaller x per ct, i.e. a slower object; a vertical line is at rest.
items.answer: Relativistic effects only appear because clocks are badly made.
items.markingKey: B. This is incorrect: Time dilation and simultaneity are properties of space-time itself, verified with atomic clocks, muons and GPS.

items.stem: Ana applies a force of 120 N to a wheel brace of length 0.4 m at 45° to the handle. Calculate the torque about the nut.
A safety poster in Vienna assumes a reaction time of 1.0 s and a braking deceleration of 7.1 m s⁻². Determine the stopping distance it should quote for a car moving at 50 km h⁻¹.
items.markingKey: A. v = 50/3.6 = 13.9 m s⁻¹ (M1); thinking distance = 13.9 m (A1); braking distance = v²/(2a) = 13.6 m (A1); total = 27.5 m.

items.stem: A teacher in Melbourne asks a class to choose the one correct statement about pressure, moles, Avogadro's constant and molar mass. Which statement should be chosen?
options: All molecules in a gas at a given temperature move at the same speed.
Boyle’s law applies even if gas leaks out of the container.
Gas pressure is caused by molecules pushing each other apart.
One mole contains the same number of particles, but masses differ: 2.0 g for H₂ and 32 g for O₂.
items.answer: One mole contains the same number of particles, but masses differ: 2.0 g for H₂ and 32 g for O₂.
items.markingKey: D. The other options are common misconceptions. One mole contains the same number of particles, but masses differ: 2.0 g for H₂ and 32 g for O₂.

items.stem: The total energy of an undamped SHM oscillator
items.answer: is constant
items.markingKey: A. Conservation of energy.

items.stem: A student in Singapore is checking notes on moment of inertia and Newton's second law for rotation. Which statement is incorrect?
options: Torque produces angular acceleration (τ = Iα); the angular velocity also depends on how long the torque acts and on the initial ω.
Like linear suvat, the rotational equations require constant angular acceleration.
Two objects with the same mass must have the same moment of inertia.
A particle moving in a straight line also has angular momentum mvr⊥ about a point not on its line of motion.
items.answer: Two objects with the same mass must have the same moment of inertia.
items.markingKey: C. This is incorrect: I depends on the distribution of mass relative to the axis, so objects of equal mass can have very different I.

items.stem: A 60 W immersion heater in boiling ethanol in a lab in Oslo evaporates 8 g of ethanol in 200 s. Determine the specific latent heat of vaporization of ethanol from these data (ignore losses).
A tuning fork of frequency 512 Hz sounds in air where the speed of sound is 330 m s⁻¹. Calculate the wavelength.

A teacher in Geneva asks a class to choose the one correct statement about displacement, velocity and acceleration as vector quantities; instantaneous and average values. Which statement should be chosen?
options: A ball thrown upwards has zero acceleration at its highest point.
Speed is a scalar (magnitude only); velocity is a vector with direction, so two objects with the same speed can have different velocities.
The equation s = ut + ½at² can be used for any motion.
At the top of its flight a projectile has zero velocity.
items.answer: Speed is a scalar (magnitude only); velocity is a vector with direction, so two objects with the same speed can have different velocities.
items.markingKey: B. The other options are common misconceptions. Speed is a scalar (magnitude only); velocity is a vector with direction, so two objects with the same speed can have different velocities.

items.stem: What is the effect of air resistance on the trajectory of a projectile?
options: The path stays a symmetric parabola
Range and maximum height are reduced and the path becomes asymmetric
items.answer: Range and maximum height are reduced and the path becomes asymmetric
items.markingKey: B. Drag removes energy and acts against velocity; descent is steeper.

items.stem: The mass of a gas in a sealed syringe stays constant while it is compressed to half its volume. Its density
items.answer: doubles
items.markingKey: B. ρ = m/V.

items.stem: During a storm near Accra, thunder is heard 2.0 s after the lightning flash. Estimate the distance to the lightning (speed of sound 340 m s⁻¹).
items.markingKey: B. d = vt (light travel time negligible) (M1) = 680 m (A1).

items.stem: A ball bearing of radius 2.0 mm moves at 0.02 m s⁻¹ through glycerol of viscosity 0.8 Pa s. Calculate the drag force using Stokes’ law.
At the top of a vertical circle the tension in a string is least because
options: the weight provides part of the centripetal force
items.answer: the weight provides part of the centripetal force
items.markingKey: A. T + mg = mv²/r.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "rolling without slipping"?
options: Motion in which the contact point is instantaneously at rest, so v = ωr
For a body in rotational equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments
The rate of change of angular displacement, ω = Δθ/Δt, in rad s⁻¹
The rate of change of angular velocity, α = Δω/Δt, in rad s⁻²
items.answer: Motion in which the contact point is instantaneously at rest, so v = ωr
items.markingKey: A. "rolling without slipping" is motion in which the contact point is instantaneously at rest, so v = ωr.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about energy balance of the Earth-atmosphere system is a common misconception? (Revision quiz set by Mei.)
options: Floating sea ice already displaces its own weight of water; sea-level rise comes mainly from thermal expansion and melting of land ice (glaciers, Greenland, Antarctica).
Ozone depletion increases UV at the surface, but the greenhouse effect is the absorption and re-emission of outgoing infrared by greenhouse gases.
N₂, O₂ and Ar, which make up 99 % of dry air, absorb almost no infrared; only molecules whose vibrations change their dipole moment are greenhouse gases.
Earth only radiates energy at night.
items.answer: Earth only radiates energy at night.
items.markingKey: D. This is incorrect: Earth radiates infrared continuously, day and night, at a rate depending on its temperature.

items.stem: An oscillator is released from rest at x = 0.04 m at t = 0 and performs SHM at 1.0 Hz. Calculate its displacement at t = 0.2 s.
A wire is replaced by one of the same material that is 0.5 times as long and has 0.5 times the diameter. By what factor does the resistance change?
A student in Vienna is checking notes on reference frames and Galilean transformations. Which statement is incorrect?
options: With ct vertical, a steeper worldline means a smaller x per ct, i.e. a slower object; a vertical line is at rest.
No forces are involved; different inertial frames measure different lengths because they disagree on simultaneity of the end-point measurements.
In her own frame everything is normal: her heartbeat and clocks run at the usual rate; it is the observer in another frame who measures her clocks running slow.
Observers in different inertial frames always agree on the velocity of an object.
items.answer: Observers in different inertial frames always agree on the velocity of an object.
items.markingKey: D. This is incorrect: Velocity depends on the frame (u′ = u − v); they agree on acceleration in Galilean relativity, not velocity.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "greenhouse effect"?
options: The fraction of incident radiation that is reflected (or scattered) by a surface or planet: total scattered power / total incident power
A process that reduces the original change, such as increased infrared emission from a warmer surface
The temperature at which a planet radiates as much power as it absorbs
The warming of a planet’s surface because atmospheric gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit part of it back towards the surface
items.answer: The warming of a planet’s surface because atmospheric gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit part of it back towards the surface
items.markingKey: D. "greenhouse effect" is the warming of a planet’s surface because atmospheric gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit part of it back towards the surface.

items.stem: A stationary bomb explodes into two fragments of masses m and 3m. The ratio of their speeds (m : 3m) is
items.markingKey: B. Equal and opposite momenta.

items.stem: The temperature of a sample of argon is raised from 500 K to 1500 K. Calculate the factor by which the rms speed of its molecules increases.
An electric winch with an efficiency of 40 % lifts a 500 kg load through 15 m in 10 s. Calculate the electrical input power.
items.markingKey: C. Useful P = mgh/t = 7360 W (M1); input = useful/efficiency = 1.84 × 10⁴ W (A1).

items.stem: A teacher in Melbourne asks a class to choose the one correct statement about series and parallel circuits and Kirchhoff's laws. Which statement should be chosen?
options: Electrons move through a wire at nearly the speed of light.
The power dissipated in a resistor always increases with its resistance.
The emf of a cell is the same as its terminal pd in all circumstances.
In series the same current flows everywhere; the pd, not the current, is shared.
items.answer: In series the same current flows everywhere; the pd, not the current, is shared.
items.markingKey: D. The other options are common misconceptions. In series the same current flows everywhere; the pd, not the current, is shared.

items.stem:
A spring launcher fires a 0.050 kg ball vertically upwards. The spring is compressed by x and the maximum height h reached by the ball above its release point is measured. Theory (no losses): ½kx² = mgh.

x / m | h / m
0.010 | 0.027
0.015 | 0.059
0.020 | 0.105
0.025 | 0.162
0.030 | 0.238
0.035 | 0.312

(a) State the quantities that should be plotted to obtain a straight line. [1]
(b) Using the data, determine the gradient of the best-fit line. [2]
(c) Hence determine the spring constant k. [1]
(d) The gradients of the maximum and minimum lines differ from the best-fit gradient by ±3 %. State k with its absolute uncertainty. [1]
items.answer: (a) h (y) against x² (x); (b) gradient ≈ 256 m⁻¹; (c) 251 N m⁻¹; (d) (251 ± 8) N m⁻¹

A loudspeaker connected to a signal generator emits sound of frequency f. The wavelength λ is found by moving a microphone between adjacent points where the signal is in phase, using a dual-trace oscilloscope. Theory: λ = v/f.

f / Hz | λ / m

500 | 0.684
600 | 0.583
800 | 0.430
1000 | 0.347
1200 | 0.288

(b) Using the data, determine the gradient of the best-fit line. [2]
(c) Hence determine the speed of sound v in air. [1]
(d) The gradients of the maximum and minimum lines differ from the best-fit gradient by ±2 %. State v with its absolute uncertainty. [1]
items.answer: (a) λ (y) against 1/f (x); (b) gradient ≈ 342 m s⁻¹; (c) 342 m s⁻¹; (d) (342 ± 7) m s⁻¹

A small blackened metal plate of surface area 0.010 m² is heated electrically in a vacuum chamber. When it reaches a steady temperature T, the electrical power P supplied equals the power radiated. Theory: P = eσAT⁴.

T / K | P / W

(b) Using the data, determine the gradient of the best-fit line. [2]
(c) Hence determine the emissivity e of the plate. [1]
(d) The gradients of the maximum and minimum lines differ from the best-fit gradient by ±4 %. State e with its absolute uncertainty. [1]

A trolley on a friction-compensated runway is pulled by a hanging mass m. The total mass of trolley plus hanging masses is kept constant by moving masses from the trolley to the hanger. The acceleration a is measured with a light gate. Theory: mg = M_total a.

accelerating force mg / N | a / m s⁻²

items.stem:
This question is about electric current, charge and potential difference.

(a) How many electrons pass a point each second in a current of 1.0 A? [2]

(b) "Conventional current flows in the same direction as electrons." Explain the flaw in this statement. [3]

(c) A wire made of aluminium, of diameter 1 mm, carries 5.0 A. The free-electron density is 6.0 × 10²⁸ m⁻³. Calculate the drift speed of the electrons. [5]
items.answer: (a) 6.25 × 10¹⁸ (b) Conventional current is defined as the flow of positive charge; electrons in metals move in the opposite direction. (c) 6.63 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] 6.25 × 10¹⁸ (A1). n = I/e. (b) [3 marks] Conventional current is defined as the flow of positive charge; electrons in metals move in the opposite direction. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (c) [5 marks] A = π(0.0005)² = 7.85 × 10⁻⁷ m² (M1); v = I/(nAe) = 6.63 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹ (A1).

items.stem:
This question is about enhanced greenhouse effect and climate change.

(a) Which is a positive feedback in the climate system? [2]

(b) Explain the difference between adaptation and mitigation. [3]

(c) A climate model uses a sensitivity parameter of 1.0 K per W m⁻². Calculate the equilibrium warming produced by a radiative forcing of 2.0 W m⁻². [5]
items.answer: (a) Melting ice reducing albedo (b) Mitigation reduces the causes of climate change (cutting emissions, carbon capture, renewables); adaptation reduces the harm of changes that occur (flood defences, drought-resistant crops). (c) 2.00 K
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] Melting ice reducing albedo (A1). It amplifies warming. (b) [3 marks] Mitigation reduces the causes of climate change (cutting emissions, carbon capture, renewables); adaptation reduces the harm of changes that occur (flood defences, drought-resistant crops). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions). (c) [5 marks] ΔT = λΔF (M1) = 2.00 K (A1).

items.stem:
This question is about energy density of fuels.

(a) Which fuel has the highest specific energy? [2]

(b) With the help of a specific example, explain why a coal-fired power station needs a continuous supply of a large mass of coal. [3]

(c) A 1000 MW power station near Nairobi burns wood (specific energy 16 MJ kg⁻¹) with an overall efficiency of 40 %. Calculate the mass of fuel burned each second. [5]
items.answer: (a) Hydrogen (≈ 142 MJ kg⁻¹) (b) Coal has a modest specific energy (~30 MJ kg⁻¹) and the station is only about 35 % efficient, so a large mass of fuel must be burned each second to supply hundreds of megawatts. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (c) 156 kg s⁻¹
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] Hydrogen (≈ 142 MJ kg⁻¹) (A1). Hydrogen releases the most energy per kg. (b) [3 marks] Award marks for: Coal has a modest specific energy (~30 MJ kg⁻¹) and the station is only about 35 % efficient, so a large mass of fuel must be burned each second to supply hundreds of megawatts. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.) (c) [5 marks] Input power = 1000/0.4 = 2500 MW (M1); m = 2500 × 10⁶/(16 × 10⁶) = 156 kg s⁻¹ (A1).

items.stem:
This question is about black-body radiation, emissivity and albedo.

(a) State what is meant by the term "emissivity". [2]

(b) Sana writes: "Clouds always cool the planet." Explain why this is inaccurate. [4]

(c) Distinguish between emissivity and albedo. [4]
items.answer: (a) The ratio of the power radiated per unit area by a surface to that radiated by a black body at the same temperature, e = P/(σAT⁴) (b) Clouds reflect sunlight (cooling) but also absorb and re-emit infrared (warming); the net effect depends on cloud type and height. (c) Emissivity describes how well a surface emits radiation compared with a black body at the same temperature; albedo is the fraction of incident radiation that a surface reflects.
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] 1 mark for the core idea: the ratio of the power radiated per unit area by a surface to that radiated by a black body at the same temperature, e = P/(σAT⁴). Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0. (b) [4 marks] Clouds reflect sunlight (cooling) but also absorb and re-emit infrared (warming); the net effect depends on cloud type and height. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (c) [4 marks] Emissivity describes how well a surface emits radiation compared with a black body at the same temperature; albedo is the fraction of incident radiation that a surface reflects. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem:
This question is about spacetime interval and spacetime (Minkowski) diagrams.

(a) Explain why events separated by a spacelike interval cannot be cause and effect. [3]

(b) On a spacetime diagram for frame S, the ct′ axis of a frame S′ moving at 0.3c is drawn. Calculate the angle between the ct and ct′ axes. [4]

(c) Explain the difference between a spacelike interval and a timelike interval. [3]
items.answer: (a) For a spacelike interval Δx > cΔt, so a signal would need to travel faster than light to link them; their time order can also be reversed in some frames. (b) 16.7° (c) A timelike interval ((cΔt)² > Δx²) can connect cause and effect and has the same time order in all frames; a spacelike interval (Δx² > (cΔt)²) cannot be bridged by any signal, and the time order of the events depends on the frame.
items.markingKey: (a) [3 marks] Award marks for: For a spacelike interval Δx > cΔt, so a signal would need to travel faster than light to link them; their time order can also be reversed in some frames. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.) (b) [4 marks] tan θ = v/c = 0.3 (M1); θ = 16.7° (A1). (c) [3 marks] A timelike interval ((cΔt)² > Δx²) can connect cause and effect and has the same time order in all frames; a spacelike interval (Δx² > (cΔt)²) cannot be bridged by any signal, and the time order of the events depends on the frame. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem:
This question is about heat engines, Carnot cycle and efficiency.

(a) Explain why the efficiency of a real engine is lower than the Carnot efficiency. [3]

(b) A student claims: "The heat rejected by a power station is a sign of poor engineering that can be eliminated." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [4]

(c) Explain the difference between a heat pump and a heat engine. [3]
items.answer: (a) Real cycles are irreversible: friction, turbulence and heat transfer across finite temperature differences increase entropy, and the processes are not ideal isotherms and adiabats. (b) Some heat rejection is required by the second law; engineering can only reduce it towards the Carnot limit (or use the waste heat in combined heat and power). (c) A heat engine uses heat flowing from hot to cold to produce work; a heat pump uses work to move thermal energy from a cold to a hot region.
items.markingKey: (a) [3 marks] Award marks for: Real cycles are irreversible: friction, turbulence and heat transfer across finite temperature differences increase entropy, and the processes are not ideal isotherms and adiabats. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.) (b) [4 marks] Some heat rejection is required by the second law; engineering can only reduce it towards the Carnot limit (or use the waste heat in combined heat and power). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (b) A student claims: "When a horse pulls a cart, the cart pulls back with an equal force, so they cannot move." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [4]

items.answer: (a) The braking force acts on the bus, not directly on passengers; by inertia (first law) their bodies continue forward until friction from seats or the floor provides a resultant force to decelerate them. (b) The equal and opposite forces act on different bodies; the horse moves because the ground pushes it forward more than the cart pulls it back. (c) The first law concerns one body: with zero resultant force its velocity is constant. The third law concerns two bodies: forces between them are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.

(b) 39.4 ± 1.4 °C (3.6 %) (c) Water has a very high specific heat capacity, so the sea warms and cools slowly, absorbing energy by day and releasing it by night and moderating the air temperature. items.answer: (a) A circuit in which components are connected end to end so that the same current flows through each (b) In series the same current flows through each and the pds add (R = R₁ + R₂); in parallel the pd is the same and the currents add (1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂). items.stem:
This question is about kinetic model of an ideal gas and the link between temperature and mean kinetic energy.

(a) With the help of a specific example, explain, using kinetic theory, why the pressure of a gas increases when it is heated at constant volume. [3]

(b) "At absolute zero an ideal gas has the greatest pressure." Explain the flaw in this statement. [4]

(c) The temperature of a sample of helium is raised from 350 K to 3150 K. Calculate the factor by which the rms speed of its molecules increases. [3]

(d) Evaluate the claim: "The kinetic theory of gases is a triumph of the scientific method." [5]
items.answer: (a) Higher temperature means a larger mean molecular speed; molecules hit the walls more often and with greater change of momentum each time, so the force per unit area increases. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (b) p ∝ T for an ideal gas, so the pressure would tend to zero as T → 0 K (real gases liquefy first). (c) 3.00 (d) It is a powerful example of a microscopic model explaining macroscopic laws, with well-understood limits (NOS: models and evidence).
items.markingKey: (a) [3 marks] Award marks for: Higher temperature means a larger mean molecular speed; molecules hit the walls more often and with greater change of momentum each time, so the force per unit area increases. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.) This question is about isovolumetric, isobaric, isothermal and adiabatic processes on p-V diagrams.

(a) Explain the difference between an isothermal process and an adiabatic process. [3]

(b) An ideal gas is taken round a rectangular cycle on a p–V diagram between pressures 1.00 × 10⁵ Pa and 2.00 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 0.00200 m³ and 0.00600 m³. Calculate the net work done per cycle. [4]

(c) A student claims: "Isobaric means no work is done." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [3]

(d) "Real processes in engines can be described accurately as isothermal or adiabatic." To what extent is this view justified? [5]
items.answer: (a) In an isothermal process T is constant, so ΔU = 0 and Q = W (heat flows in or out); in an adiabatic process Q = 0, so ΔU = −W and the temperature changes. (b) 400 J (c) Isobaric means constant pressure; work pΔV is done if the volume changes. Isovolumetric processes involve no work. (d) The idealised processes are useful models whose predictions must be corrected for real heat transfer and irreversibility.
